content.body:
**P1**  |  **Ingestion S4**  |  ~90 min

Position corrected 2026-07-30. Refusing `curl | sh` is not a policy, it is the absence of one, and it blocks adoption of a field that moves weekly. The operator's framing is right: use the open-source equivalents of JFrog Artifactory and Xray, then adopt safely. RTK was installed correctly the same day (release zip, SHA256 verified against the published checksums file, e9f2e26c...). Oak was refused because its documented install is a pipe to a shell. The difference between those two outcomes should be a process, not a mood.

## Tasks

- [ ] tools/supply/verify.py: record provenance (source URL, sha256, size, signature status, scanner verdict, decision, ts) to an append-only state/supply-chain.jsonl, and REFUSE to mark an artifact adopted with no recorded hash. Selftest plus mutation entry per the repo's four-layer convention
- [ ] Evaluate and pick from the open-source Xray equivalents: Trivy, Grype plus Syft for SBOM, OSV-Scanner, cargo-audit, cargo-deny, cargo-vet, pip-audit, and sigstore cosign with SLSA provenance for signing
- [ ] ADR stating the rule for a pipe-to-shell install: when it is acceptable, what the substitute is, and what evidence must exist before an artifact counts as adopted
- [ ] A supply_chain domain in quality-contract.json so an unverified artifact FAILS the gate rather than passing because nobody looked
- [ ] Backfill what is already installed: rtk.exe (hash on record), the claude-plugins-official marketplace clone, and whatever the WSL2 migration installs
- [ ] Then reopen Oak against a verified artifact path, because the objection was never the tool and the operator is right that we cannot avoid adopting the new scene

L-2026-07-31-b. The operator read a 5.4k-word deliverable that had passed tools/slop_lint.py and said it read as machine written, naming dashes. Measured: zero em dashes, zero en dashes, two non-ASCII characters in the file and both were quoted from the artifact under review. So the accusation was falsifiable and false, and the intuition behind it was still pointing at something the gate cannot see: hyphen-compound density 2.8 percent and sentence-length standard deviation 14.8. voice-metrics/SKILL.md:21 already classifies no-em-dashes as RULED, a decision with no corpus behind it. The harness gates the ruled proxy and leaves the measured property ungated, the same shape as L-2026-07-29-g.

## Tasks

- [ ] Port a hyphen-density and sentence-length-variance check from ~/.claude/skills/voice-metrics/voice_score.py into tools/slop_lint.py
- [ ] Fit the thresholds against the operator's own corpus (n=35,472 messages, voice-metrics profiles.json). Do not guess them; a guessed threshold is a second ruled rule wearing a number
- [ ] Regression tests in both directions: a file that passes today and reads as generated must go red, and the operator's own prose must stay green
- [ ] Mutation control proving the new check can go red, per the repo's four-layer standard
- [ ] Warn before it blocks. Collect a week of scores first, then decide the threshold from the distribution rather than from taste
- [ ] Until this lands, stop citing a clean slop_lint as evidence that prose does not read as generated. It is evidence of one banned list and one dash rule

A falsifier that cannot distinguish its stated mechanism from every other reason the same command could pass is not a falsifier.

**P2**  |  **Ingestion S4**  |  ~90 min

L-2026-07-31-c. An 11k-word review of two external artifacts presented about fifteen measured quantities in the same flat voice as its inferences. An independent recount with no access to the reasoning found four wrong, including a decimal-to-hex slip (2500134 is 262626, not 2625A6) that turned 'the anchor has no text accent colour at all' into 'it has a link colour', weakening the argument it was cited for. Separately, rendering the artifact in a browser overturned three findings derived from CSS text, one of them simply wrong about a laptop.

## Tasks

- [ ] Make the recount a step, not a virtue: any deliverable with more than five derived numbers gets a verification pass by something that cannot see the reasoning
- [ ] Any claim about a rendered artifact stays inference until rendered. The cdp path works (native Chrome 9224 with --remote-allow-origins=*) and took four minutes; there was no excuse
- [ ] A convention for marking a measured number apart from an inferred one inside a deliverable, so a reader can tell without reading a methods section
- [ ] Extend tools/refute to accept a deliverable's numeric claims as falsifiers, so a review can be re-checked by running it rather than by re-reading it
